title.zh: 卷393 列傳一百八十 李星沅 周天爵 劳崇光
title.en: Volume 393 Biographies 180: Li Xingyuan, Zhou Tianjue, Lao Chongguang
title.raw: 卷393 列傳一百八十 李星沅 周天爵 劳崇光

sentences.zh: 列傳一百八十李星沅，字石梧，湖南湘陰人。

translations.literal: Biography 180: Li Xingyuan, courtesy name Shiwu, was a native of Xiangyin in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 180 treats Li Xingyuan, whose courtesy name was Shiwu, a native of Xiangyin in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In 1832 he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and received appointment as reviser.

sentences.zh: 十五年，督廣東學政。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he supervised education in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he took charge of the provincial education commission in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 粵士多健訟，檄通省籍諸生之幹訟者，牒報诇治之，士風以肅。

translations.literal: Guangdong scholars were much given to litigation; he issued a proclamation throughout the province calling on all registered students involved in lawsuits to be reported and investigated, and scholarly conduct was thereby sobered.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese degree-holders were notoriously litigious; he circulated a province-wide order requiring local officials to report student litigants for inquiry and punishment, and academic morals tightened accordingly.

sentences.zh: 任滿，授陝西漢中知府，歷河南糧道，陝西、四川、江蘇按察使。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was appointed prefect of Hanzhong in Shaanxi, and successively served as grain intendant of Henan and surveillance commissioner of Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Upon completing his tour he became prefect of Hanzhong in Shaanxi, then grain intendant in Henan and surveillance commissioner in Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Jiangsu in turn.

sentences.zh: 在川、陝嚴治刀匪、啯匪，屢擒其魁置之法。

translations.literal: In Sichuan and Shaanxi he rigorously suppressed armed bandits and roaming desperadoes, repeatedly capturing their ringleaders and putting them to death by law.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in Sichuan and Shaanxi he cracked down hard on knife-gangs and roaming bandits, repeatedly seizing their leaders and executing them under statute.

sentences.zh: 遷江西布政使，調江蘇。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be provincial treasurer of Jiangxi, then reassigned to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Jiangxi as provincial treasurer, then transferred to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，擢陝西巡撫，署陝甘總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted governor of Shaanxi and acted as governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1842 he was elevated to governor of Shaanxi and concurrently served as acting governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，調江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to be governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1845 he was reassigned as governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢雲貴總督，兼署雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou, concurrently acting as governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1846 he rose to governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou while also acting as Yunnan governor.

sentences.zh: 先是，永昌回亂，迤西道羅天池濫殺，不分良莠，眾回益擾。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the Hui uprising in Yongchang, the Yunnan West Circuit intendant Luo Tianchi had killed indiscriminately without distinguishing good from bad, and the Hui communities grew more turbulent.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, in the Yongchang Muslim revolt, Circuit Intendant Luo Tianchi of western Yunnan had slaughtered without distinguishing loyal from rebel communities, and unrest among the Hui only worsened.

sentences.zh: 總督賀長齡、提督張必祿急於主撫，降者輒复叛。

translations.literal: Governor-General He Changling and Provincial Military Commissioner Zhang Bilu were eager to pursue appeasement; those who surrendered would rebel again.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General He Changling and Provincial Commander Zhang Bilu pressed for conciliation too hastily, so surrendered rebels repeatedly rose again.

sentences.zh: 至是，緬寧匪首馬國海被剿亡走，潛結雲州回馬登霄、海連升等復起事，迤西大震。

translations.literal: By this time Ma Guohai, bandit chief of Mienning, had been driven off in suppression and fled in hiding, secretly joining with the Yunnan Hui Ma Dengxiao, Hai Liansheng, and others to rise again; western Yunnan was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Now Ma Guohai, the Mienning rebel leader, had been routed and fled underground, secretly allying with the Yunnan Muslims Ma Dengxiao and Hai Liansheng to revolt anew, throwing the far west into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 星沅追論肇亂之由，長齡、天池並獲譴。

translations.literal: Xingyuan traced and discussed the causes of the outbreak; He Changling and Luo Tianchi were both punished.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan memorialized on the origins of the rebellion, and both He Changling and Luo Tianchi were censured.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，遣兵進剿，解散被脅回眾，首逆就殲，餘匪肅清。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he dispatched troops to advance in suppression, disbanded the Hui masses who had been coerced, the chief rebels were destroyed, and the remaining bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In 1847 he sent forces on campaign, released coerced Muslim followers, destroyed the principal rebels, and cleared out the rest.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其功，加太子太保銜，賜花翎。

translations.literal: An edict praised his merit, adding the honorary title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and bestowing peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commended his service, granting him the honorary rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the peacock feather insignia.

sentences.zh: 尋調兩江總督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to be governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reassigned as governor-general of Jiangnan and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 星沅未第時，客陶澍幕中，為掌章奏。

translations.literal: Before Xingyuan passed the examinations he had been a guest in Tao Zhu's secretariat, drafting memorials and reports.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking his degree Xingyuan had served in Tao Zhu's staff, drafting official papers.

sentences.zh: 又歷官江南，習於鹽、漕、河諸利弊。

translations.literal: Having also held office in the south, he was versed in the advantages and disadvantages of the salt, grain transport, and river conservancy systems.
translations.idiomatic: His later service in the lower Yangtze region also made him familiar with the strengths and pitfalls of salt monopoly, grain transport, and river works.

sentences.zh: 時度支告匱，廷臣主南漕改徵折色解部，於北省採買。

translations.literal: At the time the treasury reported shortages, and court officials advocated converting southern tribute grain transport to cash payments to the Board of Revenue and purchasing grain in northern provinces.
translations.idiomatic: With revenue exhausted, ministers proposed replacing southern tribute grain shipments with cash payments to the Board of Revenue and buying grain in the north.

sentences.zh: 星沅謂折多徵收不易，折少採買不敷。

translations.literal: Xingyuan said that if the conversion rate were high, collection would be difficult, and if it were low, purchases would fall short.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan argued that a high conversion rate would make collection impracticable, while a low one would leave purchases insufficient.

sentences.zh: 穀賤銀貴，民間展轉虧折。

translations.literal: Grain was cheap and silver dear, and the populace suffered repeated losses in conversion.
translations.idiomatic: With grain cheap and silver dear, ordinary people would lose heavily at every turn of exchange.

sentences.zh: 且州縣藉端浮勒，胥吏高下其手，防之皆難。

translations.literal: Moreover, prefectures and counties would seize pretexts for exactions, and clerks would manipulate rates at will—all hard to prevent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, local officials would use the change as a pretext for surcharges, and yamen clerks would manipulate figures—none of which could be effectively checked.

sentences.zh: 迭疏論列，議遂寢。

translations.literal: He submitted repeated memorials setting forth these points, and the proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized repeatedly on these points until the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 淮鹽自陶澍整頓之後，歷年又多積欠。

translations.literal: Since Tao Zhu's reorganization of Huai salt, year after year there had also been large arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tao Zhu's reforms of the Huai salt monopoly, arrears had accumulated year after year.

sentences.zh: 星沅疏陳引鹽壅積、課款支絀情形：「揆厥所由，官以畏難而因仍，商以畏難而取巧。

translations.literal: Xingyuan memorialized on the backlog of licensed salt and shortfall in revenue: "Tracing the causes, officials shrink from difficulty and let abuses continue, merchants shrink from difficulty and resort to evasions.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan described the glut of licensed salt and short revenue: "The root cause is that officials, fearing difficulty, let abuses linger, while merchants, fearing difficulty, resort to evasion.

sentences.zh: 成本增於雜費，行銷滯於售私，年復一年，幾同痼疾。

translations.literal: Costs rise through miscellaneous charges, and sales stagnate because of illicit trade; year after year it has become almost a chronic disease.
translations.idiomatic: Costs swell with surcharges and legitimate sales stall under smuggling, until the trade has become a chronic malady.

sentences.zh: 先當以內清場私，外敵鄰私，為急則治標之計。

translations.literal: First one must clear smuggling within the field and resist neighboring smuggling from without—urgent measures to treat the symptoms.
translations.idiomatic: The immediate remedy is to suppress internal smuggling and block salt from neighboring regions—emergency measures against the symptoms.

sentences.zh: 本年回空糧私，奏請查禁。

translations.literal: This year he memorialized to investigate and prohibit smuggling on returning grain boats.
translations.idiomatic: That year he also memorialized for strict prohibition of smuggling aboard returning grain transports.

sentences.zh: 其川私、墾私、潞私、浙私，均諮行堵緝。

translations.literal: Sichuan smuggling, reclaimed-land smuggling, Shanxi smuggling, and Zhejiang smuggling were all referred to the relevant authorities for blocking and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise instructed officials to interdict Sichuan, reclaimed-land, Shanxi, and Zhejiang smuggling routes.

sentences.zh: 又引船夾帶，為害最鉅，扼要搜查，於揚州仙女廟及江寧下關緝獲百餘萬斤，提省審辦。

translations.literal: Smuggling aboard licensed transport boats was the greatest harm; searches at key points at the Fairy Temple in Yangzhou and at Xia Pass in Jiangning seized more than a million jin, which were sent up for trial in the province.
translations.idiomatic: Licensed transport boats carrying contraband salt did the worst damage; searches at Yangzhou's Fairy Temple and Jiangning's Lower Pass netted over a million jin, sent up for provincial trial.

sentences.zh: 他如慎出納，提緩課，派懸引，刪繁文，配運殘引，提售新鹽，裁浮巡費，禁捏報淹銷，酌議章程八條，以圖整理。

translations.literal: Other measures included careful receipts and disbursements, advancing deferred tax quotas, assigning suspended licenses, cutting redundant paperwork, matching transport of residual licenses, promoting sale of new salt, reducing inflated patrol expenses, prohibiting false reports of delayed sales, and eight articles of regulations drafted for reorganization.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged careful accounting, advancing slow quotas, reallocating suspended licenses, cutting paperwork, moving old licenses, pushing new salt, trimming patrol costs, banning false reports of unsold stock, and eight regulatory articles for overall reform.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，下部議行。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the Board deliberated and implemented it.
translations.idiomatic: The Board received the memorial, deliberated, and put its measures into effect.

sentences.zh: 舊制，總督兼管河務，自道光二十二年後停止，至是復命兼管。

translations.literal: By old regulation the governor-general also supervised river works; this had ceased after the twenty-second year of Daoguang, but now he was again ordered to take charge.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly governors-general also oversaw river conservancy, a duty suspended after 1842 but now restored to him.

sentences.zh: 會兼署河督，疏請嚴禁廳員聚處清江，飭各歸工次。

translations.literal: As he was also acting as Director-General of Rivers, he memorialized to forbid bureau staff from gathering at Qingjiang and ordered each to return to his work station.
translations.idiomatic: While concurrently acting as Director-General of Rivers, he forbade bureau clerks from idling at Qingjiang and ordered them back to their project sites.

sentences.zh: 奏籌外海水師事宜，曰磨厲人才，曰變通營巡，曰覈實會哨，曰扼要堵緝，曰配兵足數；

translations.literal: He memorialized on coastal naval forces, proposing to train talent, reform camp patrols, verify joint inspections, block key points, and ensure full complements;
translations.idiomatic: He submitted plans for the coastal navy: develop officers, revise patrol routines, enforce joint inspections, guard choke points, and fill complements;

sentences.zh: 又請添造戰船，勸捐給獎：並允行。

translations.literal: he also requested additional war junks and rewards for charitable donations—all approved.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked for new war junks and donation incentives, all of which were approved.

sentences.zh: 俄羅斯通商舊由陸路，忽有商船至上海，執約拒之。

translations.literal: Russian trade had formerly been overland only; suddenly merchant vessels arrived at Shanghai, and he upheld the treaty and refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Russia had traded only by land routes, but when merchant ships suddenly appeared at Shanghai he held to treaty limits and turned them away.

sentences.zh: 在任兩年，宣宗甚加倚任。

translations.literal: During his two years in office the Daoguang Emperor greatly relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: In two years of service the Daoguang Emperor came to rely on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 因久病，請解職回籍，允之。

translations.literal: Because of long illness he requested leave of office and return home, which was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Prolonged illness led him to request retirement to his native place, which was granted.

sentences.zh: 三十年，宣宗崩，赴京謁梓宮，復以母老陳請歸養。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when the Daoguang Emperor died, he went to the capital to attend the coffin, then again pleaded to return home to care for his aged mother.
translations.idiomatic: In 1850, after the Daoguang Emperor's death, he went to the capital to attend the funeral rites, then again asked leave to nurse his elderly mother.

sentences.zh: 會廣西匪亂方熾，起林則徐督師，卒於途，命星沅代為欽差大臣。

translations.literal: Just then the Guangxi bandit turmoil was raging; Lin Zexu was recalled to command the campaign but died on the road, and Xingyuan was appointed Imperial Commissioner in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Guangxi rebels were flaring; Lin Zexu was summoned to command but died en route, and Xingyuan was named Imperial Commissioner to replace him.

sentences.zh: 是年十二月，抵廣西，駐柳州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year he reached Guangxi and stationed himself at Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Guangxi in the twelfth month and established headquarters at Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時左右江匪氛蔓延，諸賊尤以桂平金田洪秀全為最悍。

translations.literal: At the time bandit activity spread along the Left and Right Rivers, and among all the rebels Hong Xiuquan of Jintian in Guiping was the fiercest.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel bands now infested the Zuo and You Rivers, none bolder than Hong Xiuquan of Jintian in Guiping.

sentences.zh: 巡撫鄭祖琛、提督閔正鳳皆以貽誤黜去，週天爵、向榮繼為巡撫、提督。

translations.literal: Governor Zheng Zuchen and Provincial Commander Min Zhengfeng were both dismissed for negligence; Zhou Tianjue and Xiang Rong succeeded them as governor and commander respectively.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zheng Zuchen and Commander Min Zhengfeng were cashiered for mishandling the crisis; Zhou Tianjue and Xiang Rong replaced them as governor and provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 二人者並有重名，負意氣，議輒相左，星沅調和之，仍不協，軍事多牽掣。

translations.literal: Both men enjoyed great reputations and strong wills; their counsel constantly diverged. Xingyuan tried to reconcile them but harmony was not achieved, and military affairs were much hampered.
translations.idiomatic: Both were famous men of strong temperament whose plans constantly clashed; though Xingyuan mediated, they never cooperated, and operations suffered constant delay.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年春，向榮進剿，賊由大黃江、牛排嶺竄新墟、紫荊山。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xianfeng, Xiang Rong advanced in suppression; the rebels fled from Dahuang River and Niupai Ridge to Xinxu and Zijing Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In spring 1851 Xiang Rong pressed the attack; the rebels slipped from Dahuang River and Niupai Ridge toward Xinxu and Zijing Mountain.

sentences.zh: 星沅檄總兵秦定三、李能臣率滇、黔兵追躡，賊复竄武宣。

translations.literal: Xingyuan ordered Generals Qin Dingsan and Li Nengchen to lead Yunnan and Guizhou troops in pursuit; the rebels again fled to Wuxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan ordered Qin Dingsan and Li Nengchen with Yunnan-Guizhou troops in pursuit, driving the rebels again toward Wuxuan.

sentences.zh: 榮、天爵各進擊，賊踞東鄉，兩軍攻之不克。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong and Zhou Tianjue each advanced to attack; the rebels held Dongxiang, and the two armies failed to take them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong and Zhou Tianjue attacked separately, but the rebels held Dongxiang and both columns failed to break them.

sentences.zh: 星沅以事權不一，奏請特簡總統將軍督剿，詔斥其推諉。

translations.literal: Xingyuan, finding command authority divided, memorialized requesting appointment of a specially selected general president to direct suppression; an edict rebuked him for shirking responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing divided command, Xingyuan asked the throne to appoint a supreme field commander; the edict rebuked him for evasion.

sentences.zh: 尋命大學士賽尚阿率總兵達洪阿、都統巴清德赴湖南防堵，將以代之。

translations.literal: Soon Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a was ordered to lead Generals Da Hong'a and Banner Commander Ba Qingde to Hunan for blocking defense, intending to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a with Da Hong'a and Ba Qingde to Hunan to block the rebels, planning to replace Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿至湖南，遂授欽差大臣，赴廣西督師，命星沅回湖南治防。

translations.literal: When Sai Shang'a reached Hunan he was made Imperial Commissioner and went to Guangxi to command the army; Xingyuan was ordered back to Hunan to manage defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Sai Shang'a reached Hunan, received the Imperial Commissioner seal, and proceeded to Guangxi while Xingyuan was sent back to organize Hunan defenses.

sentences.zh: 四月，星沅力疾赴武宣前敵督戰，至則已憊甚，數日卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Xingyuan, forcing himself despite illness, went to the front at Wuxuan to direct battle; on arrival he was already exhausted, and within days he died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he dragged himself to the Wuxuan front, but was already spent on arrival and died in camp within days.

sentences.zh: 遺疏言：「賊不能平，不忠；

translations.literal: His final memorial said: "If the rebels are not pacified, that is disloyalty;
translations.idiomatic: His death memorial read: "Failure to pacify the rebels is disloyalty;

sentences.zh: 養不能終，不孝。

translations.literal: if I cannot finish caring for my mother, that is unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: failure to complete my mother's care is unfilial.

sentences.zh: 歿後斂以常服，用彰臣咎。

translations.literal: After death let me be buried in ordinary dress, to display a minister's fault."
translations.idiomatic: Bury me in plain dress after death, to mark a minister's guilt."

sentences.zh: 」文宗覽而哀之，依總督例賜卹，賜金治喪，存問其母，子二人命俟服闋引見，諡文恭。

translations.literal: The Xianfeng Emperor read it with sorrow, granted posthumous favors according to the governor's precedent, gave gold for the funeral, sent condolences to his mother, ordered his two sons to be presented after mourning, and gave the posthumous title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianfeng was moved, granted posthumous honors befitting a governor-general, funeral funds, condolences to his mother, and audience for his two sons after mourning; his posthumous title was Wengong.

sentences.zh: 子桓，官至江西布政使。

translations.literal: His son Huan rose to provincial treasurer of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huan eventually became provincial treasurer of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 週天爵，字敬修，山東東阿人。

translations.literal: Zhou Tianjue, courtesy name Jingxiu, was a native of Dong'e in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tianjue, courtesy name Jingxiu, came from Dong'e in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十六年進士，歸班銓選。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination and returned to await appointment through the Board.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in 1811 and entered the regular appointment queue.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，授安徽懷遠知縣，調阜陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang he was appointed magistrate of Huaiyuan in Anhui, then transferred to Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1824 he was named magistrate of Huaiyuan in Anhui, then moved to Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 天爵少以堅苦自立，篤信王守仁之學。

translations.literal: Tianjue from youth had stood firm through hardship and deeply believed in the learning of Wang Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Tianjue had disciplined himself through hardship and was a devoted follower of Wang Yangming's philosophy.

sentences.zh: 及為令，盡心民事，廉介絕俗，皖北盜賊橫恣，與胥吏通，天爵極刑痛懲之。

translations.literal: Once he became a magistrate he devoted himself to the people's affairs, was incorruptible beyond the common run, and when bandits ran rampant in northern Anhui in collusion with yamen clerks, Tianjue punished them with extreme severity.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate he threw himself into local affairs with austere integrity; when northern Anhui bandits colluded with clerks, he punished them with relentless severity.

sentences.zh: 有劾其殘酷者，總督蔣攸銛奏言：「天爵愛民如子，嫉惡如仇，古良​​吏也。

translations.literal: Some impeached him for cruelty; Governor-General Jiang Youshen memorialized: "Tianjue loves the people as his children and hates evil as his enemy—an excellent official of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Accusers called him cruel, but Governor-General Jiang Youshen wrote: "Tianjue loves the people as children and hates evil as an enemy—a true ancient-style official."

sentences.zh: 」由是受宣宗之知，諭曰：「不避嫌怨之員，最為難得，小過可宥之。

translations.literal: Thereby he won the Daoguang Emperor's notice; an edict said: "An official who does not shun resentment is hardest to find; small faults may be overlooked."
translations.idiomatic: The Daoguang Emperor took notice and said: "Officials who do not fear making enemies are rare; minor faults may be forgiven."

sentences.zh: 」連擢宿州知州、廬州知府、廬鳳潁泗道。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to prefect of Suzhou, prefect of Luzhou, and intendant of the Lu-Feng-Ying-Si Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to Suzhou prefect, Luzhou prefect, and intendant of the Lu-Feng-Ying-Si circuit.

sentences.zh: 所至捕盜魁，無漏網者。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he captured bandit chiefs, none escaping the net.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere he served he captured bandit leaders without exception.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢江西按察使，仍調安徽，遷陝西布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi, still transferred within Anhui, then moved to be provincial treasurer of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he became Jiangxi surveillance commissioner, was kept in Anhui service, then transferred to Shaanxi as provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 十七年，署漕運總督，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he acted as Director-General of Grain Transport, then received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1837 he acted as Director-General of Grain Transport, then received the substantive post.

sentences.zh: 時漕務積弊，運丁水手尤恣悍，特用天爵嚴馭之，劾衛官十二員以儆眾，詔褒勉之。

translations.literal: At the time the grain transport system had deep-seated abuses, and transport laborers and boatmen were especially unruly; Tianjue was specially used to discipline them strictly, impeaching twelve transport officials as a warning to all, and an edict praised and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: With transport rife with abuse and boatmen especially violent, the court used Tianjue to tighten discipline, impeaching twelve transport officers as examples, and issued commendations.

sentences.zh: 十八年，調署湖廣總督，尋授河南巡撫，擢閩浙總督，皆未行，調授湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to act as governor-general of Huguang, then appointed governor of Henan, promoted governor-general of Fujian-Zhejiang—all without taking up post—then reassigned governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 he was shifted to acting Huguang governor-general, named Henan governor and Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general without serving, then confirmed as Huguang governor-general.

sentences.zh: 漢口鎮為商船所聚，苦盜。

translations.literal: Hankou was a gathering place for merchant vessels and suffered greatly from bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Hankou, where merchant fleets gathered, was plagued by robbery.

sentences.zh: 川匪充鉛船水手，每行劫殺人；

translations.literal: Sichuan bandits served as crew on lead-transport boats and robbed and killed whenever they sailed;
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan outlaws crewed lead-transport junks and robbed and murdered along the routes;

sentences.zh: 陝、楚交界奸徒掠販婦女，並為民害：天爵捕治如律，劾失察有司及承審縱延者，悉褫其職。

translations.literal: at the Shaanxi-Huguang border scoundrels abducted and sold women—both were scourges to the people: Tianjue arrested and punished them according to law, and impeached negligent officials and those who delayed trials, stripping all of their posts.
translations.idiomatic: while Shaanxi-Huguang border gangs trafficked women—Tianjue punished all under law and cashiered negligent or dilatory officials.

sentences.zh: 荊州沿江舊於冬季委員巡緝盜賊，天爵謂屬具文，罷之；

translations.literal: Along the Jingzhou riverbank it had been the custom in winter to appoint commissioners to patrol against bandits; Tianjue said this was mere formality and abolished it;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou's winter patrol commissioners he dismissed as empty formalities;

sentences.zh: 遴幹吏暗偵，與地方官掩捕，以獲盜多寡定功過。

translations.literal: selecting capable officers for secret investigation and joint surprise arrests with local officials, judging merit and fault by the number of bandits captured.
translations.idiomatic: instead he sent capable men to spy and coordinate raids with local magistrates, rating performance by arrests made.

sentences.zh: 襄陽匪徒傳習牛八邪教，又有天主、十字各教，捕誅數十人。

translations.literal: In Xiangyang bandits propagated the Niuba heresy, and there were also Catholic and other sects; he arrested and executed several dozen.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang he suppressed the Niuba cult and Catholic and related sects, executing dozens.

sentences.zh: 每有疏陳，宣宗輒手詔褒嘉。

translations.literal: Whenever he submitted a memorial the Daoguang Emperor would personally commend him in edict.
translations.idiomatic: Each memorial drew a personal commendation from the Daoguang Emperor.

sentences.zh: 連年水災，濱江、濱漢堤垸多壞，疏請依治黃河法，遇險立挑壩，並以草護堤；

translations.literal: In successive years of flood the river and Han embankments were often breached; he memorialized to follow Yellow River practice, building emergency dikes at danger points and protecting dikes with sod;
translations.idiomatic: After repeated floods along the Yangtze and Han he urged Yellow River methods: emergency spur dikes at breaks and sod revetments;

sentences.zh: 飭治河州縣，有大工解任專治，立限保工，限內失事者罰，紳董亦如之；

translations.literal: ordering river counties and prefectures that for major works officials should be relieved to devote themselves solely to repair, with time limits and guarantees of completion, penalties for failure within the limit, and the same for local gentry managers;
translations.idiomatic: river officials facing major works were to be relieved of other duties, given deadlines and guarantees, with penalties for gentry managers as well;

sentences.zh: 漢水多灣曲，立磚石斗門以備蓄洩：並如議行。

translations.literal: the Han had many bends, so brick and stone sluice gates were built to regulate storage and release—all adopted as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: brick and stone sluice gates were built on the winding Han to regulate flow—all approved.

sentences.zh: 天爵馭吏嚴，多怨者。

translations.literal: Tianjue was strict in governing subordinates, and many bore grudges.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjue ruled subordinates harshly and made many enemies.

sentences.zh: 二十年，己革大冶知縣孔廣義揭訐多款，天爵置不問。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the dismissed Daye magistrate Kong Guangyi denounced him on many counts, and Tianjue ignored it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1840 the dismissed Daye magistrate Kong Guangyi lodged numerous charges, which Tianjue ignored.

sentences.zh: 事上聞，嚴斥之，議革職留任。

translations.literal: When the matter reached the throne he was severely rebuked and it was proposed to remove him from office while retaining him in post.
translations.idiomatic: The court learned of it, rebuked him sharply, and debated dismissal while keeping him in office.

sentences.zh: 尋言官劾天爵酷刑，與廣義言略同，命侍郎麟魁、吳其濬往按，得天爵信任候補知縣楚鏞用非刑，外委黃雲邦誣執良民諸狀，上震怒，褫天爵職，戍伊犁。

translations.literal: Soon censors impeached Tianjue for cruel punishments, much as Guangyi had said; Vice Ministers Lin Kui and Wu Qijun were sent to investigate and found that Tianjue's trusted expectant magistrate Chu Yong had used illegal torture and sub-official Huang Yunbang had falsely arrested innocent people; the emperor was greatly angered, stripped Tianjue of office, and banished him to Yili.
translations.idiomatic: Censors then echoed Guangyi's charges of torture; Lin Kui and Wu Qijun found his protégé Chu Yong torturing prisoners and Huang Yunbang framing innocents; the throne stripped him and exiled him to Yili.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，命赴廣東交靖逆將軍奕山差遣，尋免罪，留粵效力。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was ordered to Guangdong to serve under General Yishan in suppressing the British, soon pardoned and kept in Guangdong to render service.
translations.idiomatic: In 1841 he was sent to Guangdong under General Yishan against the British, soon pardoned to remain there.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，予四品頂戴，以知府候補，調江蘇辦理清江防務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was given the fourth-rank button and appointed expectant prefect, transferred to Jiangsu to manage Qingjiang coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: In 1842 he received fourth-rank insignia as expectant prefect and managed Qingjiang coastal defenses in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 海防事竣，留治淮、揚善後事宜，尋予二品頂戴，​​署漕運總督，兼署南河總督。

translations.literal: When coastal defense was finished he remained to handle Huai-Yang reconstruction, soon given the second-rank button, acting Director-General of Grain Transport, and concurrently acting Director-General of the Southern Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: After coastal work he stayed for Huai-Yang reconstruction, gained second-rank insignia, and acted as grain transport and southern river director-general.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，因濫刑及失察漕書私鐫關防，連被吏議，疏請去職，命以二品頂戴休致。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, because of excessive punishments and failure to detect a transport clerk's private carving of an official seal, he was repeatedly censured by the Board, memorialized to resign, and was ordered to retire with second-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In 1843 further charges of torture and failing to stop a clerk forging transport seals led him to resign and retire with second-rank status.

sentences.zh: 久之，廣西賊起，日益熾。

translations.literal: After a long interval Guangxi rebels arose and grew daily fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Guangxi rebels flared and grew worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 文宗御極，求知兵大臣，尚書杜受田以天爵對，遂起廣西巡撫，偕欽差大臣李星沅辦賊。

translations.literal: When the Xianfeng Emperor took the throne he sought generals versed in warfare; Minister Du Shoutian recommended Tianjue, and he was recalled as governor of Guangxi to handle rebels together with Imperial Commissioner Li Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On Xianfeng's accession the court sought experienced commanders; Du Shoutian named Tianjue, who was recalled as Guangxi governor to fight rebels with Li Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年春，親率兵與向榮會剿金田匪洪秀全等。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first Xianfeng year he personally led troops with Xiang Rong to jointly suppress the Jintian rebels Hong Xiuquan and others.
translations.idiomatic: In spring 1851 he personally led troops with Xiang Rong against Hong Xiuquan at Jintian.

sentences.zh: 賊竄武宣東鄉，合擊於東嶺村，力戰，兵有退者，天爵手刃之，援桴鼓而前，賊始卻。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to Dongxiang in Wuxuan; at Dongling Village in combined attack, after fierce fighting some soldiers retreated, and Tianjue personally killed a retreater, took the drum and advanced, and only then did the rebels withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing them to Wuxuan's Dongxiang, at Dongling Village some troops broke; Tianjue killed a fugitive himself, beat the drum, and advanced until the enemy fell back.

sentences.zh: 時懷集、賀縣及都康、下雷土司，凌雲、東蘭、橫州、博白並有匪踞，檄各屬力行團練，合力防剿。

translations.literal: At the time Huaiji, Hexian, and the Ducang and Xialei native offices, Lingyun, Donglan, Hengzhou, and Bobai all had rebels entrenched; he ordered each jurisdiction to enforce militia training and combine for defense and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels also held Huaiji, Hexian, native offices, Lingyun, Donglan, Hengzhou, and Bobai; he ordered local militia and joint suppression.

sentences.zh: 詔加天爵總督銜，專辦軍務，以布政使勞崇光攝巡撫事。

translations.literal: An edict added Tianjue the honorary governor-general rank to handle military affairs exclusively, with Provincial Treasurer Lao Chongguang acting as governor.
translations.idiomatic: He received honorary governor-general rank for military command while Lao Chongguang acted as governor.

sentences.zh: 天爵年近八旬，每戰親臨前敵，惟與李星沅、向榮皆不協。

translations.literal: Tianjue was nearly eighty and went to the front in every battle, yet he was at odds with Li Xingyuan and Xiang Rong alike.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly eighty, he still led from the front, yet clashed with both Li Xingyuan and Xiang Rong.

sentences.zh: 星沅既疏請特簡總統督師，尋病歿，命天爵暫署欽差大臣。

translations.literal: After Xingyuan had memorialized for a specially selected supreme commander and soon died of illness, Tianjue was ordered temporarily to act as Imperial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingyuan's plea for a supreme commander was followed by his death, Tianjue briefly acted as Imperial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賊由武宣竄象州，詔斥天爵等相持日久，不能制賊，褫總督銜，解軍務，回省暫署巡撫。

translations.literal: When the rebels fled from Wuxuan to Xiangzhou, an edict rebuked Tianjue and others for prolonged stalemate and failure to subdue the rebels, stripped his governor-general rank, relieved him of military duties, and returned him to the province temporarily as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: As rebels slipped to Xiangzhou, the court rebuked the stalemate, removed his honorary rank and command, and left him acting governor only.

sentences.zh: 洎賽尚阿至軍，議復不合，自陳衰病，詔命來京。

translations.literal: When Sai Shang'a arrived at the army their counsel again clashed; he reported his infirmity, and an edict ordered him to come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sai Shang'a's arrival renewed discord; citing illness, he was summoned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 既至，連召對十一次，極言軍事，文宗為之動容，然方倚賽尚阿，亦未盡用其言。

translations.literal: Once there he was summoned to audience eleven times and spoke exhaustively on military affairs; the Xianfeng Emperor was moved, but as he still relied on Sai Shang'a he did not fully adopt Tianjue's views.
translations.idiomatic: He was received eleven times and spoke frankly on strategy; the emperor was impressed but, still relying on Sai Shang'a, did not fully follow his advice.

sentences.zh: 二年，粵匪擾及兩湖，天爵僑居宿州，命偕安徽巡撫蔣文慶治防務。

translations.literal: In the second year Guangdong rebels disturbed the Two Huguang provinces; Tianjue was living in exile in Suzhou and was ordered to assist Anhui Governor Jiang Wenqing in managing defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 Cantonese rebels threatened Huguang; Tianjue, living in Suzhou, was ordered to help Anhui Governor Jiang Wenqing organize defenses.

sentences.zh: 三年，疏陳廬、鳳為江淮要區，赴正陽關撫舊捻張鳳山等一千二百人用之，請江蘇、山東、安徽、河南舉行團練。

translations.literal: In the third year he memorialized that Luzhou and Fengyang were key points of the Jiang-Huai region, went to Zhengyang Pass to win over the old Nian bandit Zhang Fengshan and twelve hundred men for use, and requested that Jiangsu, Shandong, Anhui, and Henan conduct militia training.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 he argued that Luzhou-Fengyang guarded the Jiang-Huai corridor, recruited twelve hundred Nian followers under Zhang Fengshan at Zhengyang Pass, and urged militia training in four provinces.

sentences.zh: 未幾，安慶陷，文慶死之。

translations.literal: Before long Anqing fell and Wenqing died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Anqing fell and Jiang Wenqing was killed.

sentences.zh: 命天爵署安徽巡撫，尋實授。

translations.literal: Tianjue was ordered to act as governor of Anhui, then received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjue was named acting Anhui governor, then confirmed in office.

sentences.zh: 江寧亦陷，天爵請扼黃河杜賊北竄，辭巡撫專任兵事。

translations.literal: Jiangning also fell; Tianjue requested to hold the Yellow River to block the rebels' northward flight, resigned the governorship to devote himself solely to military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing fell too, he asked to seal the Yellow River against northern rebel advances and gave up the governorship for full-time command.

sentences.zh: 命以兵部侍郎銜督師剿宿州、懷遠、蒙城、靈壁捻匪。

translations.literal: He was ordered to command suppression of Nian bandits in Suzhou, Huaiyuan, Mengcheng, and Lingbi with the honorary rank of Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He received Vice Minister of War rank to campaign against Nian rebels in northern Anhui.

sentences.zh: 北路漸清，進規廬、鳳，擒定遠捻首陸遐齡，散其眾四千餘，被褒賚。

translations.literal: The northern route was gradually cleared; he advanced toward Luzhou and Fengyang, captured the Dingyuan Nian chief Lu Xialing, dispersed more than four thousand of his followers, and was rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Clearing the north, he moved on Luzhou-Fengyang, captured Nian leader Lu Xialing, dispersed four thousand followers, and earned imperial praise.

sentences.zh: 疏論廬州知府胡元煒劣跡，請革職逮治，巡撫李嘉端置不問。

translations.literal: He memorialized on the misconduct of Luzhou Prefect Hu Yuanwei and requested dismissal and arrest; Governor Li Jiaduan ignored it.
translations.idiomatic: He denounced Luzhou Prefect Hu Yuanwei and demanded arrest; Governor Li Jiaduan did nothing.

sentences.zh: 元煒通賊內應，廬州陷，江忠源死之。

translations.literal: Yuanwei colluded with the rebels as an inside agent; Luzhou fell and Jiang Zhongyuan died.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yuanwei turned traitor from within; Luzhou fell and Jiang Zhongyuan was killed.

sentences.zh: 粵匪踞臨淮關，天爵外遏來賊，內清土匪，孤軍支拄。

translations.literal: Guangdong rebels held Linhuai Pass; Tianjue blocked incoming enemies without and cleared local bandits within, holding on alone with a solitary army.
translations.idiomatic: With Cantonese rebels at Linhuai Pass, he fought external invaders and internal bandits almost alone.

sentences.zh: 方奉命往援廬州，以疾卒於軍。

translations.literal: Just as he was ordered to relieve Luzhou, he died of illness in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to relieve Luzhou, he died of illness on campaign.

sentences.zh: 上震悼，詔嘉其秉性忠直，勇敢有為，心地品行迥超流俗，追贈尚書銜，依贈官賜卹，特諡文忠，不由內閣擬上；

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply grieved; an edict praised his upright loyal nature, courage and enterprise, and character far above the common run, posthumously granting the honorary title of Minister and posthumous favors according to donated-office precedent, with the special posthumous title Wenzhong conferred without going through the Grand Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: The throne mourned him, praising his loyalty, courage, and uncommon integrity, granting posthumous ministerial rank and special burial honors under the posthumous title Wenzhong without Grand Secretariat review;

sentences.zh: 擢其子光碧都司，賜光岳舉人。

translations.literal: his son Guangbi was promoted to garrison commander, and Guangyue was granted juren status.
translations.idiomatic: his son Guangbi became a garrison commander and Guangyue received juren degree status.

sentences.zh: 勞崇光，字辛陔，湖南善化人。

translations.literal: Lao Chongguang, courtesy name Xingai, was a native of Shanhua in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Lao Chongguang, courtesy name Xingai, came from Shanhua in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as Hanlin bachelor, and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In 1832 he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，出為山西平陽知府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he went out as prefect of Pingyang in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1841 he was posted as prefect of Pingyang in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 調太原，擢冀寧道，遷廣西按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Taiyuan, promoted intendant of Jining Circuit, and moved to be surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Taiyuan, he became Jining intendant and then Guangxi surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，奉使赴越南冊封。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was sent on mission to invest the king of Vietnam.
translations.idiomatic: In 1848 he led the investiture mission to Vietnam.

sentences.zh: 事竣入關，值匪亂，駐思恩、南寧，督軍進剿。

translations.literal: When the mission ended and he entered the border, bandit turmoil had broken out; he stationed at Si'en and Nanning and directed troops in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Returning through the border during unrest, he based himself at Si'en and Nanning to direct suppression.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，遷湖北布政使，未行而湖南賊李沅發起新寧，仍留廣西治防。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was moved to be provincial treasurer of Hubei, but before taking up post Li Yuanfa of Hunan rose in Xinning, and he was kept in Guangxi for defense.
translations.idiomatic: In 1849 he was named Hubei treasurer, but Li Yuanfa's Hunan revolt kept him in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 沅發平，敘功賜花翎。

translations.literal: When Yuanfa was pacified, merit was recorded and peacock feathers were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanfa's defeat he received peacock feathers for his service.

sentences.zh: 三十年，就授廣西布政使。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he received substantive appointment as provincial treasurer of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1850 he was confirmed as Guangxi provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 慶遠賊竄武緣、賓州，崇光偕提督向榮會剿。

translations.literal: Rebels from Qingyuan fled to Wuyuan and Binzhou; Chongguang joined Provincial Commander Xiang Rong in joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan rebels raided Wuyuan and Binzhou; Chongguang campaigned with Xiang Rong.

sentences.zh: 擒賊首陳勝，又平上林、遷江竄匪，設方略解散匪黨凡數十起。

translations.literal: He captured the bandit chief Chen Sheng, also pacified fleeing bandits in Shanglin and Qianjiang, and by strategy dissolved bandit factions in several dozen cases.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Chen Sheng, cleared Shanglin and Qianjiang bands, and dissolved dozens of rebel cells by policy.

sentences.zh: 撫張家祥收隸部下，改名國樑，後以戰功顯。

translations.literal: He won over Zhang Jiaxiang to his command, renamed him Guoliang, who later distinguished himself in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited Zhang Jiaxiang, renamed him Guoliang, who later became a noted field commander.

sentences.zh: 尋署巡撫，副將伊克坦布戰歿於桂平，檄總兵周鳳岐赴援。

translations.literal: Soon he acted as governor; Vice Commander Yike Tanbu died in battle at Guiping, and he ordered General Zhou Fengqi to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: Acting as governor, he sent Zhou Fengqi to relieve Guiping after Yike Tanbu fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 時命李星沅督師，週天爵為巡撫專治軍。

translations.literal: At the time Li Xingyuan was ordered to command the army and Zhou Tianjue was governor devoted to military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xingyuan then commanded the campaign while Zhou Tianjue handled military affairs as governor.

sentences.zh: 崇光仍攝巡撫事，會辦軍務。

translations.literal: Chongguang still acted as governor and jointly handled military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chongguang continued as acting governor on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，大學士賽尚阿代星沅，而鄒鳴鶴繼為巡撫，崇光會辦如故，平西林、博白、懷集竄賊。

translations.literal: In the first Xianfeng year Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a replaced Xingyuan, and Zou Minghe succeeded as governor; Chongguang continued joint duty as before and pacified fleeing rebels in Xilin, Bobai, and Huaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 Sai Shang'a replaced Xingyuan and Zou Minghe became governor; Chongguang cleared Xilin, Bobai, and Huaiji rebels.

sentences.zh: 廣東賊顏品瑤擾南寧、太平，崇光駐兵南邕，與廣東軍合擊，屢戰皆捷，品瑤就殲，又平貴縣賊，被優敘。

translations.literal: Guangdong rebel Yan Pinyao harassed Nanning and Taiping; Chongguang stationed troops at Nanyong and joined Guangdong forces in attack, winning repeated battles; Pinyao was destroyed, rebels in Guixian were also pacified, and he received preferential recognition.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Pinyao of Guangdong threatened Nanning; Chongguang at Nanyong allied with Guangdong troops, destroyed Yan, pacified Guixian, and earned commendation.

sentences.zh: 偕左江鎮總兵谷韞燦平白山賊，舉行南、太、泗、鎮四府團練，殲顏品瑤餘黨於靈山，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: With Zuojiang garrison commander Gu Yuncan he pacified Baishan rebels, instituted militia in the four prefectures of Nanning, Taiping, Si, and Zhen, destroyed Yan Pinyao's remnants at Lingshan, and received the first-rank official button.
translations.idiomatic: With Gu Yuncan he cleared Baishan, organized militia in four prefectures, wiped out Yan's remnants at Lingshan, and gained first-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 二年，駐梧州，會廣東軍剿艇匪。

translations.literal: In the second year he stationed at Wuzhou and joined Guangdong forces in suppressing boat bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he based at Wuzhou to fight boat pirates with Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 尋金田賊洪秀全等永安突圍出犯桂林，命崇光回援，至則賊已北竄，連陷興安、全州，偕總兵和春追擊之，賊遂入湖南。

translations.literal: Soon the Jintian rebels Hong Xiuquan and others broke out of Yong'an and attacked Guilin; Chongguang was ordered back to relieve the city, but on arrival the rebels had already fled north, successively taking Xing'an and Quanzhou; with General He Chun he pursued, and the rebels then entered Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Xiuquan broke from Yong'an toward Guilin, Chongguang returned too late; the rebels had fled north through Xing'an and Quanzhou into Hunan despite pursuit with He Chun.

sentences.zh: 會雲貴總督吳文鎔疏稱崇光有膽略血性，請重其事權，就擢巡撫。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Wu Wenrong memorialized that Chongguang had courage, strategy, and fighting spirit, requesting heavier authority, and he was promoted governor on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wenrong praised his courage and secured his immediate promotion to governor.

sentences.zh: 上疏略曰：「桂林雖解圍，賊氛不遠，群情尚復驚疑，增兵置防，皆非倉卒能辦。

translations.literal: His memorial in summary said: "Although Guilin's siege was lifted, rebel activity is not far off and public feeling remains alarmed; increasing troops and defenses cannot be done hastily.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Guilin is relieved but danger remains; troops and defenses cannot be improvised.

sentences.zh: 惟就現有兵力佈置，省標調赴各處者，次第撤回，駐防城內，遴選練丁分扼城外要隘。

translations.literal: Only with existing forces should disposition be made: provincial standard troops sent elsewhere should be recalled in turn to garrison the city, and selected militia should hold key passes outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Deploy existing forces, recall provincial detachments, garrison the city, and post trained militia at outer passes.

sentences.zh: 激勵團練以作民氣，招撫流亡以復民力，訓練兵勇以肅軍紀，搜緝土匪以靖內奸。

translations.literal: Encourage militia to raise popular morale, win back refugees to restore popular strength, train soldiers to tighten military discipline, and search out local bandits to quiet internal traitors.
translations.idiomatic: Rally militia, resettle refugees, drill troops, and hunt local bandits.

sentences.zh: 各屬遊匪、土匪不時蠢動，額兵不敷分撥，鼓舞團練，以資捍衛而備援剿。

translations.literal: In each jurisdiction roaming and local bandits stir from time to time; regular troops are insufficient for distribution; rouse militia to aid defense and prepare for relief suppression.
translations.idiomatic: With regulars overstretched, rely on militia for defense and reserve suppression."

translations.literal: " [End of memorial.]
translations.idiomatic: Thus concluded his memorial.

sentences.zh: 時賽尚阿既黜，崇光專任廣西軍務，詔以匪雖已出粵境舊巢穴，慮渠魁踞之為回竄地步，責以搜捕黨羽。

translations.literal: At the time Sai Shang'a had already been dismissed; Chongguang had sole charge of Guangxi military affairs; an edict said that although the bandits had left their old nests in Guangdong territory, fearing the chiefs might occupy them as bases for return, he was charged to search out and capture accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: After Sai Shang'a's dismissal Chongguang held Guangxi command alone; the court warned that abandoned rebel nests might become return bases and ordered pursuit of accomplices.

sentences.zh: 三年，洪秀全等既踞江寧，分黨北犯中原。

translations.literal: In the third year, after Hong Xiuquan and others had seized Jiangning, they sent parties north to invade the central plains.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853, with Nanjing taken, Taiping forces pushed north into the heartland.

sentences.zh: 兵事日棘，朝廷不暇顧及邊遠，廣西伏莽時起，旋滅旋萌，餉絀兵單，惟恃團練，不能大創賊。

translations.literal: Military affairs grew daily more urgent; the court had no leisure to attend to remote borders; hidden rebels in Guangxi rose repeatedly, extinguished and sprouting again; funds were short and troops few, relying only on militia, unable to inflict major defeats on the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: As the central crisis deepened, Guangxi was neglected; local uprisings flickered on depleted revenues and thin armies, with militia alone unable to crush rebels.

sentences.zh: 崇光且剿且撫，支拄數載。

translations.literal: Chongguang both suppressed and appeased, holding on for several years.
translations.idiomatic: For years Chongguang alternated suppression and conciliation to hold the province.

sentences.zh: 洎英人踞廣州後，廣東賊氛复熾。

translations.literal: When the English occupied Guangzhou afterward, rebel activity in Guangdong flared again.
translations.idiomatic: After the British seized Guangzhou, Guangdong unrest revived.

sentences.zh: 艇匪竄擾廣西，潯州、柳州、慶遠、梧州、南寧相繼陷。

translations.literal: Boat bandits raided Guangxi; Xunzhou, Liuzhou, Qingyuan, Wuzhou, and Nanning fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Boat pirates overran Guangxi; Xunzhou, Liuzhou, Qingyuan, Wuzhou, and Nanning fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 近地土匪益起，屢逼桂林。

translations.literal: Local bandits near the capital rose increasingly and repeatedly threatened Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby bandits repeatedly menaced Guilin.

sentences.zh: 軍中多降將，心皆叵測。

translations.literal: The army had many surrendered generals, all of doubtful loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Many surrendered commanders in his ranks were unreliable.

sentences.zh: 崇光乞師於湖南，七年，駱秉章令蔣益澧率湘軍赴援，屢破賊，復興安、靈川，入屯省城，乃誅反側，易守軍，桂林始安。

translations.literal: Chongguang begged troops from Hunan; in the seventh year Luo Bingzhang ordered Jiang Yili to lead Hunan Army reinforcements, repeatedly defeating rebels, recovering Xing'an and Lingchuan, entering to garrison the provincial city, then executing the disloyal, replacing the garrison, and only then was Guilin secure.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 Jiang Yili's Hunan Army arrived, retook Xing'an and Lingchuan, secured the capital by purging traitors and reforming the garrison.

sentences.zh: 八年，奏留益澧在廣西勦賊，連擊艇匪於平樂令公渡、五塘，大破之，斬馘萬餘，由是艇匪始衰，慶遠、柳州相繼复。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he memorialized to retain Yili in Guangxi for suppression; repeatedly attacking boat bandits at Linggongdu in Pingle and Wutang, he inflicted a great defeat and beheaded more than ten thousand; thereafter boat bandits began to decline and Qingyuan and Liuzhou were recovered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he kept Jiang Yili, smashed boat pirates at Pingle and Wutang killing ten thousand, and recovered Qingyuan and Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 九年，調廣東巡撫，兼署兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred governor of Guangdong, concurrently acting governor-general of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he became Guangdong governor and acting governor-general of Guangdong-Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 英軍猶踞省城，前任總督黃宗漢、巡撫耆齡等，皆駐外縣不敢入。

translations.literal: British forces still held the provincial capital; former Governor-General Huang Zonghan, Governor Qiling, and others all stayed in outer counties and dared not enter.
translations.idiomatic: The British still held Guangzhou; Huang Zonghan and Qiling camped outside the city in fear.

sentences.zh: 崇光至，坦然入城，與敵軍狎居。

translations.literal: When Chongguang arrived he calmly entered the city and lived on familiar terms with the enemy forces.
translations.idiomatic: Chongguang entered openly and lived alongside the occupation forces.

sentences.zh: 尋實授總督，迭遣將禦湖南、江西竄匪，擊走之。

translations.literal: Soon he received substantive appointment as governor-general and repeatedly sent generals to repel rebels fleeing from Hunan and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Confirmed as governor-general, he drove off Hunan and Jiangxi raiders.

sentences.zh: 本境土寇時起，皆不久撲滅。

translations.literal: Local bandits within the province rose from time to time but were all soon suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial bandit flare-ups were quickly put down.

sentences.zh: 與廣西軍會剿艇匪，梧州、潯州賊匪漸清。

translations.literal: Joining Guangxi forces in suppressing boat bandits, Wuzhou and Xunzhou rebels were gradually cleared.
translations.idiomatic: With Guangxi allies he cleared Wuzhou and Xunzhou pirates.

sentences.zh: 至十一年，英法聯軍犯京師，和議成，廣州敵軍始退。

translations.literal: By the eleventh year the Anglo-French allied forces attacked the capital; after peace was made the Guangzhou enemy forces at last withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861, after the allied attack on Beijing and peace talks, foreign troops finally left Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，以失察都司陶昌培、知縣許慶鎔營私納賄，降三級調用，命仍以一品頂戴赴貴州按事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, for failure to detect Battalion Commander Tao Changpei and Magistrate Xu Qingrong taking bribes for private gain, he was demoted three ranks and transferred, but was ordered still to proceed to Guizhou on investigation with first-rank button.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was demoted for overlooking bribery by Tao Changpei and Xu Qingrong, yet sent to Guizhou with first-rank status.

sentences.zh: 前巡撫耆齡、御史華祝三復劾崇光任用非人，調度乖方，詔命自陳，下署總督晏端書、提督昆壽察按，得免議。

translations.literal: Former Governor Qiling and Censor Hua Zhu thrice impeached Chongguang for employing unfit men and erratic command; an edict ordered him to explain himself; Acting Governor-General Yan Duanshu and Commander Kun Shou investigated and he was exempted from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Charges of bad appointments by Qiling and Hua Zhu led to self-defense and investigation, ending in exoneration.

sentences.zh: 尋授雲貴總督。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general.

sentences.zh: 雲南自總督潘鐸被戕，巡撫徐之銘結回酋以自保，張凱嵩繼署總督，久不至，以規避黜，命崇光代之。

translations.literal: Since Governor-General Pan Duo had been killed in Yunnan, Governor Xu Zhiming had allied with Hui chiefs for self-protection; Zhang Kaisong succeeded as acting governor-general but long failed to arrive and was dismissed for evasion; Chongguang was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: After Pan Duo's murder Xu Zhiming relied on Muslim chiefs; Zhang Kaisong's delayed arrival cost him the post, and Chongguang replaced him.

sentences.zh: 崇光至貴州，會粵匪石達開餘黨陷綏陽，督兵擊走之，遂駐貴陽。

translations.literal: Chongguang reached Guizhou; coincidentally remnants of the Guangdong rebel Shi Dakai's party took Suining; he directed troops to drive them off and then stationed at Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Guizhou he repelled Shi Dakai's remnants from Suining and based at Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 三年春，土匪、苗匪屢來犯，偕巡撫張亮基勒兵固守，賊敗退。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year local bandits and Miao bandits repeatedly attacked; with Governor Zhang Liangji he urged the troops to hold firm and the rebels were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In spring 1864 he and Zhang Liangji beat back repeated Miao and bandit assaults on Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 時雲南叛回猶雜處省城，議者皆言不可遽往。

translations.literal: At the time rebellious Hui still mixed in the Yunnan provincial capital; advisers all said he should not go hastily.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers warned against entering Yunnan while Muslim rebels still held the capital.

sentences.zh: 崇光迳行，軍民父老喜，迎於郊，回眾始稍斂。

translations.literal: Chongguang went straight there; soldiers and civilians, elders and youth rejoiced, welcoming him in the suburbs, and the Hui masses at last grew somewhat restrained.
translations.idiomatic: He went anyway; the populace welcomed him and even Hui communities quieted.

sentences.zh: 逆首馬榮、馬連升踞曲靖為巢穴。

translations.literal: Rebel leaders Ma Rong and Ma Liansheng held Qujing as their lair.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chiefs Ma Rong and Ma Liansheng entrenched themselves at Qujing.

sentences.zh: 崇光知候補道岑毓英、降回總兵馬如龍可用，四年春，令參將馮世興與二人合師攻克曲靖，擒榮、連升等斬以徇，遂收馬龍、尋甸，迤東肅清，遣提督趙德光克平江外賊巢，复廣順，進克貴州，黔西大定。

translations.literal: Chongguang knew that expectant circuit intendant Cen Yuying and surrendered Hui regional commander Ma Rulong could be used; in the spring of the fourth year he ordered Battalion Commander Feng Shixing to join the two in combined force to capture Qujing, seized Rong, Liansheng, and others and executed them as a warning, then recovered Malong and Xundian, pacified eastern Yunnan, sent Provincial Commander Zhao Deguang to level bandit nests beyond the rivers, recovered Guangshun, advanced to take Guizhou, and stabilized western Guizhou at Dading.
translations.idiomatic: Using Cen Yuying and Ma Rulong, in 1865 he took Qujing, executed Ma Rong and Ma Liansheng, cleared eastern Yunnan, and extended operations into Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，复普洱及思茅，雲南軍事漸利。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Pu'er and Simao were recovered and Yunnan military affairs gradually improved.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 Pu'er and Simao were recovered and the Yunnan front turned favorable.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒，優詔賜卹。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died; a favorable edict granted posthumous favors.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1867 with full posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 嘉其「沈毅有為，歷官兩廣、雲貴，皆不避艱險，俾地方日有起色」，贈太子太保，諡文毅。

translations.literal: He was praised for being "steady and resolute in action; in office in the Two Guangs and Yunnan-Guizhou he never shunned hardship, enabling the regions day by day to improve," and was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised his steadfast service in Guangdong, Guangxi, and the southwest, granting Grand Guardian rank and the posthumous title Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 廣西請建專祠，雲、貴祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: Guangxi requested a special temple for him; Yunnan and Guizhou enshrined him in the temples of eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi built him a special shrine; Yunnan and Guizhou placed him among notable officials.

sentences.zh: 論曰：粵匪之起也，始由疆臣玩誤，繼復將帥不和。

translations.literal: The commentary says: When the Guangdong rebels arose, at first frontier officials were negligent, and afterward generals were not in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Cantonese rebellion began with negligent governors, then divided commanders.

sentences.zh: 李星沅、週天爵皆素以忠勤著，文宗採時譽而付以重任，於軍事皆不得要領。

translations.literal: Li Xingyuan and Zhou Tianjue were both known for loyalty and diligence; the Xianfeng Emperor chose them on contemporary reputation and entrusted heavy responsibility, yet in military affairs neither grasped the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xingyuan and Zhou Tianjue enjoyed reputations for loyalty, yet neither mastered war when Xianfeng entrusted them.

sentences.zh: 及易以賽尚阿，而敗壞益甚，虎兕出柙，遂不可製矣。

translations.literal: When they were replaced by Sai Shang'a the ruin grew worse; tigers and rhinoceroses broke from their pens and could no longer be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Replacing them with Sai Shang'a only worsened the collapse, as rebels broke loose beyond control.

sentences.zh: 勞崇光久在兵間，洪秀全北竄後已不顧舊巢，然伏莽四起，終賴湘軍之力，數年而後克定；

translations.literal: Lao Chongguang was long amid warfare; after Hong Xiuquan fled north he no longer cared for the old nest, yet hidden rebels rose on all sides and only after several years with Hunan Army strength was the region finally pacified;
translations.idiomatic: Lao Chongguang endured years of war; after Hong Xiuquan left Guangxi, local rebels still required Hunan Army aid for years before order returned;

sentences.zh: 其於廣東、雲南皆受事於萬難措置之時，履虎不咥，權略有足稱焉。

translations.literal: in Guangdong and Yunnan he took office at times when nothing could be easily arranged; treading on a tiger's tail without being bitten, his resourcefulness was worthy of note.
translations.idiomatic: yet in Guangdong and Yunnan he took impossible posts and survived by shrewd command—no small achievement.
